newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Irish airline Ryanair joins Irish/US stock exchanges.
newsitem.headline: Irish airline Ryanair joins Irish/US stock exchanges.

text.p: Ireland's 'low-budget' airline Ryanair announced on Tuesday that it was seeking to float on the Irish stock exchange and the New York Nasdaq, the first Irish company to seek a simultaneous quote both sides of the Atlantic.

Ryanair is offering approximately 54.2 million shares at an offer price of between 165 Irish pence ($2.46) to 195 Irish pence this gives the company a market capitalisation of between 261.2 million Irish pounds ($389.4 million) to 308.7 million Irish pounds.
"Our secret is low fares, low fares and even more low fares. No meals, no frills, no newspapers, no nuts," chief executive Michael O'Leary told reporters at the announcement of the flotation.
Ryanair, which has been operating for 12 years and has a fleet of 17 Boeing 737-200 aircraft, said the funds from the share offer will be used to cut debt which is currently 35 million Irish pounds.
It will also to allow the airline to be in a position to buy aircraft when necessary, it said.
Speculation that the company would seek a listing mounted after U.S. entrepreneur David Bonderman became Ryanair chairman in December 1996 after taking the 20 percent stake in the airline.

Bonderman took over from former GPA chief Tony Ryan whose family founded Ryanair. After the offering the Ryan family will own 35.3 percent of the company down from 61.7 percent prior to the offer. While Irish Air and chief executive Michael O'Leary will own 15.7 and 14.1 percent respectively.
The flotation will comprise an offer of shares to investors in Ireland, a public offer in the U.S. and offers to professional investors in the UK and Continental Europe, Ryanair said
Ryanair said its strategy was to aim for 20 to 30 percent sales growth per annum and raise the flight frequencies on existing routes.
It said it had increased and aircraft order of six aircraft to eight aircraft from Lufthansa which it said would give it seat capacity growth.
Morgan Stanley & Co International Ltd have been appointed Global co-ordinator and bookrunner for the issue.
The offering will be underwritten by Morgan Stanley, Investment Bank of Ireland, CS First Boston and the Robinson Humphrey Company, Inc.
Morgan Stanley and IBI Corporate Finance will act as joint sponsors and financial advisers to Ryanair and Davy Stockbrokers will be brokers to the issue.
